# ivue@2.5.0 — definePropTypes, the Static re-wrap fix, private banned

<p class="release-head"><a class="release-gh" href="https://github.com/infinite-system/ivue/releases/tag/ivue%402.5.0" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">View on GitHub ↗</a><span class="release-date">Released August 31, 2026</span></p>

Feature release, zero breaking runtime changes. Three stories: the
props-contract system gets its missing piece (`definePropTypes`, and
defaults maps that no longer need `Omit`), `Static()` fixes a re-wrap
bug in deep subclass chains, and the shipped standard hardens — every
override says `override`, `private` is banned, and a runnable gate
enforces the rules in CI.

### Added

- **`definePropTypes(types)`** — an identity helper for prop-TYPES
  maps. A bare object const widens `required: true` to `boolean`;
  generic inference through this call preserves the literal, which the
  defaults check below depends on. One call, zero runtime cost.
- **`ExtractPropDefaultTypes` filters required props.** Props declared
  `required: true` can never carry a default, so they no longer appear
  in the defaults map's type. The `Omit<...>` wrappers that stripped
  them by hand die; a deliberately default-free optional prop is
  declared `key: undefined` — the ruling stated in the defaults object
  itself. Together with `propsWithDefaults` this completes the
  extensible contract system: types, defaults, and the merged props
  object are plain namespace data a subclass composes by spread. The
  [Extensible Components](https://ivue.dev/guide/extensible-components)
  guide is the full reference.

### Fixed

- **`Static()` re-wrapping a subclass could resurrect a parent-bound
  method.** The wrap walk treated an already-wrapped ancestor's
  bind/cache symbol properties as API and re-installed them on the
  child, where the child's own chain lookup expected to bind for
  itself. The walk now recognizes every bind/cache symbol the module
  ever issues — registered and unregistered alike — and skips its own
  runtime residue. Double-wrapped subclass chains bind correctly.

### The standard (ships in the tarball — `npx ivue skill`)

The operating manual grew four rulings since 2.4.0, each mirrored at
[ivue.dev/guide/standard](https://ivue.dev/guide/standard):

- **One seam per module.** A class file holds exactly three residents:
  imports, the class, the namespace — in Identity → Values → Types
  order. File-private values are non-exported namespace members.
- **Two-tier props contracts.** Small surfaces author the contract
  inline in the namespace; large ones author it in a sibling
  `XProps.ts` that the namespace re-exports 1:1. Consumers read the
  namespace either way.
- **Overrides say so out loud.** `noImplicitOverride` is on and every
  overriding member carries `override` — a base rename breaks every
  subclass at the exact member instead of silently orphaning it.
- **`private` is banned.** Visibility is a three-tier statement of
  audience: `public` for consumers, `protected` for subclasses,
  `private` for nobody. The reasoning is the
  [Ban private](https://ivue.dev/blog/ban-private) post.

- **A runnable gate.** `skills/ivue/ivue-standards-check.ts` checks a
  tree against the standard from the command line (`npm run gate`
  wires it in this repo), with a JSON skip list for rulings, a
  `bootstrapCli` seam that makes a house-specific subclass gate three
  getters and one line, and an opt-in `GeneratorStandard` extension
  carrying the invariant-methodology checks.

### Measured

Engine: **1,146 B gzipped** (`gzip -c dist/index.es.js | wc -c`).
Tests: **209 passing, 100% coverage on every metric** (statements,
branches, functions, lines) across `Reactive.ts`, `Static.ts`,
`ivue.ts`, `kernel.ts`, `extras.ts`, `LazyShared.ts`, `index.ts`.
